summary_of_bug: Caverphone is applying the special "mb" rule to the start of the string instead of only to the end. The failing test shows "mb" should encode to M111111111 and "mbmb" to MPM1111111, but the current implementation incorrectly rewrites leading "mb" as if it matched the spec’s end-of-name rule.

CODEC-115.label: P
CODEC-115.reason: Regional signal exists because DoubleMetaphone is in the same `org.apache.commons.codec.language` package as Caverphone, so it points to the phonetic-encoding subsystem. But the mechanism is unrelated: this is about field visibility/API design (`maxCodeLen` access level), not string transformation rules or prefix/suffix handling. Useful only as weak neighborhood context.

CODEC-114.label: P
CODEC-114.reason: Also in the same `org.apache.commons.codec.language` area, and specifically another phonetic encoder (`Soundex`), so it gives slight regional context. However, the issue is about constant visibility/protection (`US_ENGLISH_MAPPING`), not encoding logic or incorrect rule application. No shared faulty mechanism beyond being in the same subsystem.

CODEC-111.label: I
CODEC-111.reason: This is in `org.apache.commons.codec.net.URLCodec`, a different subsystem from phonetic encoders in `org.apache.commons.codec.language`. The mechanism is also unrelated—constant mutability/finality versus incorrect suffix rule implementation in string encoding. It provides essentially no localization value.
